Synopsis:
    Gaza's hospitals and civilian population face a deepening energy crisis driven by acute shortages of engine oil, diesel and generator spare parts. With no grid electricity since October 2023 and an October 2025 ceasefire failing to ease humanitarian conditions, hospital generators are operating well beyond safe maintenance intervals, endangering patients. Private electricity costs have surged ~20-fold, leaving most of Gaza's ~2 million displaced residents unable to afford power. Israel's COGAT cites oversight mechanisms, while MSF warns of rising mortality risk. The crisis shows no near-term resolution.

Relevance: NO — The article focuses exclusively on Gaza's humanitarian energy crisis. It has no connection to EU energy markets, TTF gas, or German power.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 15 — The Gaza energy and humanitarian crisis has been extensively documented since late 2023. This article adds granular detail (oil price surge to $1,300/litre, generator maintenance intervals extended 4x) but confirms a well-established and ongoing situation with no new market-relevant uncertainty.
